evidence: Hor. S. 2.4.65: pingue merum, rich wine (Lewis & Short s.v. pinguis)
terms.comment: A description of ours, from two classical words: mollis, soft and smooth, and pinguis, fat, rich, used by Horace of rich wine and plump figs. No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for creamy; cremum itself is late, and Traupman’s cremō fartus is cream-filled (see “cream-filled”).

phrases.latin: Quam molle et pingue hoc gelātum est!
phrases.english: How creamy this ice cream is!
With some cream in it the soup will be creamier.

sources: Lewis & Short: mollis · Lewis & Short: pinguis
